title: One fret: a half step
summary: Measure the smallest move along a string.

steps.title: The smallest move
steps.body:
A **half step**, also called a semitone, is the distance from one fret to the next on the same string. Open to fret 1 is also a half step. Move towards the body to go higher, or towards the headstock to go lower.

**Why it matters:** Counting one-fret moves helps you measure how notes fit together.

steps.title: B to C is one fret
steps.body: On string 5, B at fret 2 and C at fret 3 are a half step apart. The letters change, but there is no extra fret between them.

items.prompt: Play A2, then go up a half step. Use the lit positions.

steps.title: Move one fret at a time
steps.body: Choose a string. Pluck a comfortable fret, then the next fret towards the body. Listen to the small rise. Go back one fret to hear the same distance down.

items.prompt: How far apart are these two notes?
Play A2 at fret 5 on string 6, then go down a half step.
